newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Key events in the latest refugee crisis in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Key events in the latest refugee crisis in Zaire.

text.p: Hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees have left their camps in eastern Zaire and headed for home since Friday.
Here is a chronology of major events in the Zaire refugee crisis leading up to the U.N. decision to dispatch a multinational force, still planned despite the exodus of refugees.

Oct 7 - Deputy governor of Zaire's South Kivu province tells 300,000-strong Banyamulenge community -- ethnic Tutsis settled in the region for generations -- to leave Zaire within a week or "be hunted down as rebels". The warning sparks a revolt.
Oct 21 - Fighting between rebels and Zairean troops disrupts life in camps housing 1.2 million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees. Aid agencies report up to 250,000 refugees on the move.
Oct 24 - Rebels seize their first sizeable town, Uvira on the northern shore of Lake Tanganyika.
Oct 29 - U.N. refugee agency says the situation in eastern Zaire is now desperate, says it has lost contact with more than half a million refugees who fled the fighting.
Oct 30 - Rebels capture Bukavu, capital of South Kivu province, amid scenes of slaughter. Bukavu's Roman Catholic archbishop is among the dead.
Nov 1 - Fierce fighting for Goma, capital of North Kivu province, reaches a peak. Rebels backed by Rwandan army soldiers gain control after battles in which about 500 people die.
Nov 2 - International aid workers flee Goma, leaving the refugees in east Zaire without U.N. support and assistance.
Nov 4 - President Mobutu Sese Seko, who has not been in Zaire since August, leaves Switzerland after cancer treatment for the French Riviera.
Nov 5 - Eight African countries hold summit in Nairobi, call for neutral military force to go to Zaire to help refugees.
Nov 6 - Foreign minister of France, the most enthusiastic backer of an intervention force in Zaire, accuses international community of being "spineless" in its response to the Zaire refugee crisis.
Nov 7 - War refugees trickle into Rwandan border town of Gisenyi, bringing first witness accounts of the suffering. They say people who fled camps are dying of thirst on barren, waterless mountains.
Nov 9 - Security Council asks U.N. secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali to lay the groundwork for a multilateral force to help end the crisis, says he should report back by November 20.
Nov 10 - Pressure mounts on the U.N. to move with greater sense of urgency. European Union aid commissioner Emma Bonino accuses Security Council of scandalous indifference.
Nov 12 - Canada offers to lead the international force to provide humanitarian aid.
Nov 13 - U.S President Bill Clinton agrees in principle to order U.S. troops to participate "in limited fashion".
Nov 14 - Rebels bombard Mugunga, the biggest refugee camp, with rockets, mortar and heavy artillery for six hours.
Nov 15 - Thousands of frightened Rwandan refugees surge out of Mugunga and other camps and head for home. Five abreast, they move across the horizon and into the Rwandan town of Gisenyi.

The huge movement of people solves the thorny problem of how to separate the refugees from the Hutu fighters in their midst, but the U.N. Security Council goes ahead with approval of the deployment of a Canadian-led multinational force until March 31.
Nov 17 - U.N. officials say about 250,000 Rwandan refugees cross the border into Rwanda in the first two-and-a-half days of the exodus.
